_comment: Assertions over the example application folder — the fixture for the apply/render/prep
lane. Offline and deterministic: no model, no network.
Two kinds of assertion live here.
Conformance — the fixture matches the templates the skills ship. Required frontmatter
keys are read out of the template files themselves, so a template that grows a slot
fails the fixture until the fixture grows it too, and the templates stay load-bearing
Trip-wires — claims the fixture TEMPTS an artifact into repeating, and the rule that
stops each one. Every trip-wire asserts the temptation is really present (`must_appear`)
as well as absent from the outputs. A fixture with no trap teaches nothing, and an
assertion over a trap that has been quietly deleted passes forever. `must_appear` is
matched against the QUOTED inbound text only — lines beginning with `>` — because the
claim is the trap and the fixture's own commentary about the claim is not.
`documented_by` tethers each group to the sentence in examples/README.md that explains it.
Delete the sentence and the group fails as untethered.
Patterns are Python regexes, matched case-insensitively.

documented_by.event-vocabulary: the whole thread as a dated event log
documented_by.artifact-frontmatter: Every artifact says which corpus it came from.

inbox_claims.rule: apply rule 2 / render rule 1 — _inbox/ is never evidence, and a recruiter's account of the team's remit is a claim by a stranger with an incentive
inbox_claims.why: The panel knows what their own team does. Repeating the recruiter's number back to them is a sentence the candidate has to defend and cannot.
must_appear: everything downstream of the booking API
forbidden: everything downstream of the booking api
inbox_claims.documented_by: The recruiter's claims never become facts.

inbox_claims.rule: apply rule 2 — attributed employer context may aim the prep, never become fact
inbox_claims.why: Whether the seat is new and what headcount comes with it are the recruiter's selling points. Planning out loud around either one asserts something nobody has verified.
inbox_claims.documented_by: The recruiter's claims never become facts.

inbox_claims.rule: prep — a recruiter is selling a job; their account of the state of the systems tells you what to prepare for and never what is true
inbox_claims.why: A candidate who walks in believing the build is already modernised has prepared for a different job, and says so in the first five minutes.
inbox_claims.documented_by: The recruiter's claims never become facts.

gap.rule: apply's fit check — papering over a no-corpus-evidence requirement with the nearest adjacent story
gap.why: Mentoring two juniors is the obvious cover for a line-management requirement and it survives exactly one follow-up question. When it goes, the four strong requirements above it get discounted with it.

03-story-bank.md: Nothing in the corpus backs this section

gap.documented_by: The adjacent story is right there and nothing reaches for it.
